California is the most populated sub-national entity in North America. If it were an independent country, California would rank 38th in population in the world. It has a larger population than <Australia> and <Canada>.[[6]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-6) Its population is one third larger than that of the next most populous state, <Texas>.[[7]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-7) California surpassed [New York](New_York_(state) "New York (state)") to become the most populous state in 1962.[[8]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-Pat_Brown_Bio-8) California's population growth has slowed dramatically in the 21st century.[[9]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-9)[[10]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-10) In 2010, the state's five most populous counties were [Los Angeles County](Los_Angeles_County "Los Angeles County"), [San Diego County](San_Diego_County "San Diego County"), [Orange County](Orange_County%2C_California "Orange County, California"), [Riverside County](Riverside_County "Riverside County"), and [San Bernardino County](San_Bernardino_County "San Bernardino County"), with Riverside County having the largest percentage increase in population.[[11]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-11) The [largest metro areas in California](List_of_California_urban_areas "List of California urban areas"), as of 2010, are [Los Angeles](Los_Angeles_metropolitan_area "Los Angeles metropolitan area"), [San Francisco](San_Francisco%2C_California "San Francisco, California")-[Oakland](Oakland%2C_California "Oakland, California")-[San Jose](San_Jose%2C_California "San Jose, California"), [San Diego](San_Diego_Metro "San Diego Metro"), [Riverside-San Bernardino](Inland_Empire "Inland Empire"), and [Sacramento](Sacramento%2C_California "Sacramento, California").[[12]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-12) From 2006 until 2016, the state lost a net population of about 1 million people from emigration to other states,[[13]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-13) yet the population of the state continued to grow due to immigration from overseas and more births than deaths.[[14]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-14)

As of 2006, California had an estimated population of 37,172,015, more than 12 percent of the U.S. population. This includes a natural increase since the last census of 1,557,112 people (i.e., 2,781,539 births minus 1,224,427 deaths) and an increase due to net migration of 751,419 people. Immigration resulted in a net increase of 1,415,879 people, and migration from within the U.S. resulted in a net decrease of 564,100 people. California is the 13th fastest-growing state. As of 2023 the total fertility rate was 1.52 which is on par with Canada.[[15]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-15)

The [center of population](Center_of_population "Center of population") of <California> is located at  [35°27′49″N 119°19′31″W﻿ / ﻿35.463595°N 119.325359°W﻿ / 35.463595; -119.325359](geo:35.463595,-119.325359) in [Kern County](Kern_County%2C_California "Kern County, California"), near the town of [Shafter](Shafter%2C_California "Shafter, California").[[16]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-16)

No single ethnic group forms a majority of California's population, making the state a [minority-majority state](Minority-majority_state "Minority-majority state"). Hispanics (of any race) are the largest single ethnic group in the state.[[17]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-17) [Spanish](Spanish_language_in_California "Spanish language in California") is the state's second most widely spoken language. Areas with especially large Spanish speaking populations include the [Los Angeles metropolitan area](Los_Angeles_metropolitan_area "Los Angeles metropolitan area"), the [California-Mexico border](Mexico%E2%80%93United_States_border "Mexico–United States border") counties of [San Diego](San_Diego_County "San Diego County") and [Imperial](Imperial_County%2C_California "Imperial County, California"), and the [San Joaquin Valley](San_Joaquin_Valley "San Joaquin Valley"). Nearly 43% of Californian residents speak a language other than English at home, a proportion far higher than any other state.[[18]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-18)

In 2011, there were an estimated 2.6 million [undocumented immigrants](Illegal_immigration_to_the_United_States "Illegal immigration to the United States") residing in California.[[19]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-19) California is home to almost 25% of the country's undocumented population, making up 6% of California's residents overall. Two-thirds of California's undocumented population have lived in the state for more than 10 years.[[20]](Demographics_of_California#cite_note-20)

The **demographics of Asian Americans** describe a [heterogeneous](Homogeneity_and_heterogeneity#Heterogeneity "Homogeneity and heterogeneity") group of people in the [United States](United_States "United States") who trace their ancestry to one or more [Asian](Asia "Asia") countries.[[1]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-1)[[2]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-2)[[3]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-C4WDefault-10.1353/dsp.1991.0014-3)

[Manilamen](Filipinos "Filipinos") began to reside in Louisiana as the first Asian Americans to live in the continental in the United States.[[4]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-Saint_Malo-4) Most Asian Americans have arrived after 1965.[[5]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-T2012-5) These individuals make up one-quarter of all immigrants who have arrived in the U.S. since 1965, and 59% of Asian Americans are foreign-born.[[6]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-PewApr2010-6) During the [2010 United States Census](2010_United_States_Census "2010 United States Census") the largest ethnic groups were [Chinese American](Chinese_American "Chinese American"), [Filipino Americans](Filipino_Americans "Filipino Americans"), [Indian Americans](Indian_Americans "Indian Americans"), [Vietnamese Americans](Vietnamese_Americans "Vietnamese Americans"), [Korean Americans](Korean_Americans "Korean Americans"), and [Japanese Americans](Japanese_Americans "Japanese Americans").[[7]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-PCT7_2010USC-7)

The [2020 United States Census](2020_United_States_Census "2020 United States Census") reported approximately 19.9 million people identified as Asian alone in 2020. Adding in the 4.1 million respondents who identified as Asian in combination with another race group, the Asian American population comprised 24 million people (7.2% of the total population).[[8]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-2020census-improved-composition-8)

The overall population is highly urbanized[[9]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-Lott2004-9) and is concentrated in the [West Coast of the United States](West_Coast_of_the_United_States "West Coast of the United States") and [New York metropolitan area](New_York_metropolitan_area "New York metropolitan area").[[6]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-PewApr2010-6) Generally, Asian Americans are well educated,[[10]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-CensusEdu2003-10) and Asian American households have higher average incomes.[[11]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-IPHICUS2005-11) However, socioeconomic status is not uniform among their population.[[12]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-WeingartenSmith-12) Asian Americans hold diverse religious views, with substantial numbers being religiously unaffiliated or secular, Christian, [Hindu](Hinduism "Hinduism"), and [Muslim](Islam "Islam").[[13]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-PewRPL2008-13) About 4-5% of Asian Americans identify as LGBT.[[14]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-LGBT-14)[[15]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-15)

## Background

Main articles: [History of Asian Americans](History_of_Asian_Americans "History of Asian Americans") and [History of Asian American immigration](History_of_Asian_American_immigration "History of Asian American immigration")

The first recorded Asian Americans in the continental United States were a group of [Filipino](Filipino_people "Filipino people") men who established the small settlement of [Saint Malo, Louisiana](Saint_Malo%2C_Louisiana "Saint Malo, Louisiana"), after fleeing mistreatment aboard [Spanish](New_Spain "New Spain") [ships](Manila_galleon "Manila galleon").[[4]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-Saint_Malo-4) Since there were no women with them, the <Manilamen>, as they were known, married <Cajun> and [Native American](Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas "Indigenous peoples of the Americas") women.[[16]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-16) In 1778, [Chinese](Chinese_people "Chinese people") and [European](Europe "Europe") explorers [first arrived](First_contact_(anthropology) "First contact (anthropology)") in <Hawaii>.[[17]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-17)[[18]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-18) Numerous Chinese and [Japanese](Japanese_people "Japanese people") began immigrating to the US in the mid-19th century;[[19]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-19) numerous Chinese immigrants worked as laborers on the [First transcontinental railroad](First_transcontinental_railroad "First transcontinental railroad"), many who immigrated due to overpopulation and poverty experienced in [Canton Province](Canton_Province "Canton Province").[[20]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-20) In the mid-20th century, [refugees](Refugees "Refugees") from [Southeast Asia](Southeast_Asia "Southeast Asia") fled wars in the homelands to come to the United States.[[21]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-21) Most Asian Americans who immigrated to the United States arrived after 1965, due to [immigration reform](Immigration_and_Nationality_Act_of_1965 "Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965") that ended an [earlier era of exclusion of Asian immigrants](Asian_immigration_to_the_United_States "Asian immigration to the United States").[[5]](Demographics_of_Asian_Americans#cite_note-T2012-5)
